prompt:
I need the front end for Innlab. A training version of hotel reservations and front-office software for college hospitality-management programs, which instructors set up to mirror their own teaching inn and the practice scenarios students work through.

Who's using it: Gwen Abernathy, the front-office instructor in a community college hospitality program that runs a real 12-room teaching inn on campus. She managed front desks at two downtown hotels before teaching and knows rate management well, but she sets the system up only twice a year.

What they're doing right now: The spring cohort of 26 students starts in six weeks and she is configuring the system for the term. The inn was renovated over the summer: two rooms were combined into a suite and one room is now accessible with a roll-in shower, so the room inventory is out of date. She wants to add a new 'graduation weekend' rate with a two-night minimum and a stricter cancellation policy, retire the old 'parents' weekend' package, and set which practice scenarios unlock in which week (walk-ins and overbookings in week 3, group blocks in week 7, rate disputes and no-show charging in week 10). She also wants first-term students to be unable to override rates or waive fees, while second-term students can, with a reason.

What's in the system at this point: Inn: Tamarack House, 12 rooms (now 11 after combining 204 and 205 into Suite 204): 6 queen, 3 double-double, 1 accessible king (room 101), 1 suite; each with floor, max occupancy, bed type, features and a base rate ($119–$229). 5 current rate plans (Standard, AAA, Faculty, Parents' Weekend package, Extended Stay 5+ nights) with prices, date ranges, minimum stays, cancellation windows (24h, 72h, nonrefundable) and deposit rules. A proposed Graduation Weekend rate for May 15–17. 14 practice scenarios with titles, difficulty, and the week they unlock. Student roles: First-term Desk Agent (19 students), Second-term Shift Lead (7 students), each with allowed actions such as override rate, waive late checkout fee, move reservation, issue refund. Tax settings: 11% lodging tax plus $2 city occupancy fee per night. Last term's settings saved for comparison.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
